newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European airline traffic increased in 1996.
newsitem.headline: European airline traffic increased in 1996.

text.p: Passenger traffic carried by major European airlines rose seven percent year-on-year in 1996 due to consistently higher growth in long-haul travel, the Association of European Airlines (AEA) said on Tuesday.
Growth in passenger-kilometres, the industry's key measure of travel volume, was even higher at 8.1 percent for the year, it said.

Load factor was a new record at 70.4 percent. The group said, however, that a drop in the intra-European load factor of 0.4 percent to 61 percent was a "disappointment". The load factor for long-haul travel was up half a point at 74.8 percent.
AEA said that the airfreight market was less buoyant than passenger travel, rising by 4.3 percent in the year.
Good growth in the Far East was offset by a slight drop in North Atlantic freights.
"The result was that, for the first time, Eastern routes overtook the North Atlantic as AEA's largest freight market in tonne-km terms," it said.
